    Lines & septal thickening — quick reference

    Smooth septal thickening — thin, uniform lines with no architectural distortion. Classic for hydrostatic/permeability interstitial edema, early lymphangitic carcinomatosis, pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (with superimposed ground-glass — "crazy paving"), and some lymphoproliferative disease.

    Irregular septal thickening (reticulation) — coarse, distorted lines, usually with intralobular septal thickening and traction bronchiectasis. The signature of fibrosis — UIP/IPF and fibrotic connective-tissue-disease-associated ILD.

    Subpleural sparing — a relatively specific sign for NSIP, distinguishing it from UIP, which is typically subpleural- and basal-predominant.

    Anatomical distortion (traction bronchiectasis/bronchiolectasis, architectural distortion) — marks irreversible fibrotic disease rather than a reversible process such as edema or infection.

    General teaching framework — provided as a reference for interpreting the categories tested here, not a case-specific diagnosis. Sub-interlobular pattern is only assessed when interlobular septal thickening is present.
